newsitem.title: PERU: Shell says to decide Camisea gas partner in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Shell says to decide Camisea gas partner in Q3.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group said Thursday it would decide in the third quarter, between consortia led by Vector S.A. and Fluor Daniel, a partner to develop the infrastructure for its Camisea gas-fields in Peru.
"The decision will be taken in the third quarter of 1997," Shell's Murray Jones, manager for security and environment, told reporters at a gas conference in Lima.
"The investment with the association is estimated at $2.5 billion," he added.

Jones added the Vector-led consortium also included Brazil's Odebrecht S.A. and local construction firm Grana y Montero. Fluor Daniel's consortium includes Peru's Cosapi and an Argentine company Jones declined to name.

"At this moment, Vector and Fluor Daniel have presented individual plans on how they would wok with Shell in the development of the gas, including the construction of a pipeline, the transport and the operation of the gas," he said.
"The two proposals are very big and are being evaluated by a Shell team assigned for this."

Royal Dutch/Shell, together with operating partner Mobil, is at the half-way point of a two-year licence to study the Camisea reserves in Peru's eastern jungle, estimated to contain seven times the total in the rest of the country.
It hopes to produce gas from 1999 and be transporting the fuel to Peru's coast, 300 miles (500 km) away, before 2002.
Jones added that Shell Prospecting Development Peru had already signed some agreements for marketing the gas. But he did not give details.

Since the beginning of the Camisea project, Shell had invested between $60 million and $70 million in exploratory wells, Jones also said. "We plan to finish the exploratory wells in April 1998. Then we will make the first evaluation well in Block 75."
Ron McCoy, development director for gas marketing at Mobil Exploration and Producing Peru, said two possible routes were being investigated for bringing the gas produced at Camisea to Peru's coast.
